script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

A bustling community center. CLIFF, a grizzled old coach, presides over a rowdy group of elderly men gathered around a table, engaged in a heated card game.

CLIFF
(yelling)
I've got a full house, boys! Seventies, eighties, and a pair of jokers!

The room erupts in laughter. Suddenly, the door swings open.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - HALLWAY - CONTINUOUS

BEN, a shy, quiet man in his seventies, enters the hallway, looking lost. He catches sight of Cliff and hesitates.

EXT. COMMUNITY CENTER - PARKING LOT - CONTINUOUS

Ben sits alone on a bench, watching the sun set as Cliff approaches.

CLIFF
Hey there, old friend. I couldn't help but notice you weren't at cards today. You alright?

BEN
Just a bit down, Cliff. My wife, Marge, passed away last week. I don't really feel like joining in the fun anymore.

CLIFF
(puts a hand on Ben's shoulder)
I'm sorry for your loss, Ben. But Marge wouldn't have wanted you to mope around, would she?

BEN
(smiling)
No, I suppose she wouldn't.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

The following day, Ben hesitantly enters the community center to find Cliff waiting for him.

CLIFF
(excitedly)
Great! You've decided to join us, huh? We've got something new to try out today.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - GYM - DAY

Ben is introduced to a group of elderly men engaged in a spirited game of table tennis.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - CAFETERIA - LATER

The group gathers for lunch, and Ben finds himself sitting next to BOB, an old friend.

BOB
(friendly)
Hey there, Ben. Long time no see! How's Marge?

Ben's eyes fill with tears, and he looks away.

BOB
(concerned)
I'm so sorry, old friend. I didn't mean to bring that up.

BEN
(voice shaking)
It's alright, Bob. It's been a rough week.

CLIFF
(cheerfully)
Hey, guys, why don't we switch things up a bit? Let's go for a walk around the park. Get some fresh air.

EXT. COMMUNITY CENTER PARK - DAY

The group gathers for their weekly walk, and Ben finds himself in a lively conversation with a fellow participant, CHARLIE.

CHARLIE
(laughing)
Hey, Ben, ever tried your hand at gardening? My wife and I have a beautiful little patch in the backyard.

BEN
(smiling)
No, I haven't. Marge and I weren't really the gardening type.

CHARLIE
Well, perhaps it's time to start a new hobby. You know what they say - new beginnings and all that.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - GYM - DAY

The following week, Ben arrives at the community center to find the table tennis court transformed into a makeshift greenhouse.

CLIFF
(excitedly)
Surprise! We've started our very own community garden. Come, Ben, I've got a perfect spot for you.

Ben hesitantly joins in, and soon finds himself lost in the camaraderie of planting and nurturing new life.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - CAFETERIA - WEEKS LATER

The group gathers for their weekly lunch, and Ben proudly shows off the progress of the community garden.

BOB
(admiringly)
That's quite a transformation, Ben! I'm glad you've found something to keep you busy.

BEN
(smiling)
It's been wonderful, Bob. I feel like I've really found a new family here.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - GYM - DAY

Months pass, and the community garden flourishes, with Ben becoming an integral part of the group.

CLIFF
(teary-eyed)
I'm so proud of all of you. You've really turned this place into a home for so many.

BEN
(smiling)
We couldn't have done it without you, Cliff.

FADE OUT.

THE END
